items.text: Explain what a TypeScript union type is. Include a short markdown table with two rows, one TypeScript code block and one bash code block. Keep it under 200 words. Do not use any tools.

A **union type** lets one value be one of several types. You write it with the `|` operator. TypeScript then only lets you use members that every type in the union shares. To use anything more specific, you first narrow the type with a check such as `typeof`, `in`, or a discriminant property.

| Union | Allowed values |
|-------|----------------|
| `string \| number` | `"hello"`, `42` |
| `"on" \| "off"` | Only the literals `"on"` or `"off"` |

```typescript
type Id = string | number;

function formatId(id: Id): string {
  if (typeof id === "number") {
    return id.toFixed(0); // narrowed to number
  }
  return id.toUpperCase(); // narrowed to string
}

formatId(7);      // "7"
formatId("abc");  // "ABC"
```

Unions are useful for function parameters that accept more than one input shape. They're also good for modeling states like `"loading" | "success" | "error"`, and for expressing nullable values such as `User | null`.

To type-check a file:

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit union-demo.ts
```
